# A route's markup is built at compile time, so anything it renders has to be a
# literal or an expression over something known per request.

# A window's URL template declares vars -- `/p/{pkg}` puts `pkg` in scope
# for the body. Those are known per request exactly as state is, so markup over
# one renders into a hole rather than being refused.
sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out_param param.sngl
grep 'HandleFunc' out_param/server.go

-- param.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

component main {
    window #pkg(title="t", href="/p/{pkg}") {
        html.a(href="/p/" + pkg, innerText=pkg)
    }
}
